task_2.title: Adopt inclusive boundary control for date range APIs
task_2.description: The update adds an `inclusive` parameter to xarray date range creation APIs and starts deprecating `closed` to align with pandas. Users can now explicitly choose both, neither, left-only, or right-only boundary inclusion, while existing `closed` usage continues to work temporarily with a deprecation warning.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that date range creation supports the new `inclusive` boundary-selection behavior while preserving existing `closed` behavior only as a deprecated compatibility path.

expectation.grounded: `xarray.date_range()` and `xarray.cftime_range()` must accept a new `inclusive` parameter with supported values `both`, `neither`, `left`, `right`, and `None`. When `inclusive` is omitted or passed as `None`, the produced range must behave as fully inclusive on both boundaries. The existing `closed` parameter must remain accepted for compatibility, emit a `FutureWarning`, and map as follows: `None` to `inclusive='both'`, `left` to `inclusive='left'`, and `right` to `inclusive='right'`. Passing an invalid `closed` value must raise `ValueError`. Passing deprecated `closed` together with a non-`None` `inclusive` value must raise `ValueError`. Boundary filtering must be reflected in the returned values for both standard-calendar and CFTime-based range generation.
expectation.conceptual: Range-construction APIs should let users choose whether the start and end boundaries are included using a single modern `inclusive` option. Existing callers using `closed` should continue to get equivalent results for now, but they should receive a deprecation warning and be prevented from combining old and new boundary arguments in the same call.

constraints.grounded: Default calls without `inclusive` or `closed` must remain behaviorally equivalent to fully including both endpoints. `inclusive=None` must be treated the same as `inclusive='both'`. Deprecated `closed` compatibility must not alter returned values compared with the corresponding `inclusive` setting. Validation must reject unsupported `inclusive` or `closed` values through `ValueError`, and mixed `closed` plus explicit `inclusive` usage must fail instead of silently choosing one. The behavior must remain consistent across `date_range()` and `cftime_range()`.
constraints.conceptual: The upgrade must preserve existing default range results, provide a clean migration path from the old option to the new one, and fail clearly on ambiguous or unsupported boundary selections. The same boundary rules should apply regardless of which date range variant a user calls.

behavior: `inclusive='both'` returns ranges with both start and end boundaries included when those boundaries fall on the generated frequency.
`inclusive='neither'` excludes both boundaries from the returned range.
`inclusive='left'` includes the start boundary and excludes the end boundary.
`inclusive='right'` excludes the start boundary and includes the end boundary.
Omitting `inclusive` or passing `inclusive=None` yields the same result as full inclusion on both sides.
Using `closed=None`, `closed='left'`, or `closed='right'` continues to produce the corresponding range values but emits a `FutureWarning` because `closed` is deprecated.
Passing both deprecated `closed` and an explicit non-`None` `inclusive` value raises `ValueError`.
Passing an unsupported `closed` value raises `ValueError`.
acceptance_criteria: When a caller creates a range with `inclusive='both'`, it should include both matching boundary timestamps in the result.
When a caller creates a range with `inclusive='neither'`, it should omit both matching boundary timestamps from the result.
When a caller creates a range with `inclusive='left'` or `inclusive='right'`, it should include only the requested boundary side.
When a caller omits `inclusive` or passes `inclusive=None`, it should receive the same values as `inclusive='both'`.
When a caller uses `closed=None`, `closed='left'`, or `closed='right'`, it should receive a `FutureWarning` and the same range values as the equivalent `inclusive` setting.
When a caller passes both `closed` and an explicit non-`None` `inclusive` value, the call should fail with `ValueError`.
When a caller passes an invalid `closed` value, the call should fail with `ValueError`.
The same acceptance checks should hold for both `xarray.date_range()` and `xarray.cftime_range()`.

task_3.title: Support concatenating datasets with missing data variables
task_3.description: The upgrade changes xarray dataset concatenation so datasets no longer need identical data-variable sets. xarray.concat() now includes variables that appear in only some inputs and fills the missing portions in the concatenated result, while preserving deterministic variable ordering and continuing to reject missing coordinates where coordinate participation requires consistency.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that concatenating datasets can succeed even when some datasets omit data variables that exist in others, without requiring callers to pre-create placeholder variables, while keeping coordinate consistency checks and predictable output layout.

expectation.grounded: xarray.concat() should accept Dataset inputs whose data_vars differ across members and include the union of eligible data variables in the result. For data variables missing from one or more inputs, the concatenated output should contain those variables with the absent segments filled using the concat fill_value semantics. This behavior should apply for normal array-valued variables and scalar data variables that are expanded by concatenation. Variable ordering should remain deterministic based on order of appearance across the provided datasets. Coordinates that are expected to participate in concatenation, including cases driven by coords='all' or similar coordinate inclusion rules, should still raise ValueError when a required coordinate is absent from any dataset.
expectation.conceptual: Concatenation should behave like an outer union for data variables: users can combine datasets with non-identical variable sets and still get one result containing all relevant variables, with missing portions represented as missing data. The result should be stable in layout and should continue to fail when coordinate definitions are incomplete for a requested coordinate-aware concat.

constraints.grounded: Do not require identical data_vars across all datasets as a precondition for xarray.concat(). Preserve existing coordinate validation behavior by continuing to error on missing required coordinates instead of silently fabricating them. Preserve concat fill behavior across dtypes through fill_value handling, including numeric, string/object-like, integer promoted to support missing values, datetime64, and timedelta64 results. Preserve deterministic variable order according to first appearance in the dataset sequence. Concatenating empty datasets should remain valid.
constraints.conceptual: The change should relax dataset variable matching only where users expect optional data variables, not weaken coordinate integrity checks. Missing values should appear in a type-appropriate way, output ordering should stay predictable, and previously valid empty or partially populated concatenations should remain safe.

behavior: Concatenation includes data variables that are present in only a subset of input datasets.
Missing segments for absent data variables are filled in the concatenated result rather than causing failure.
The fill behavior follows the concat fill_value setting and remains observable across supported dtypes.
Scalar or non-concat-dimension data variables can be expanded into the concatenated dimension when concat settings require them to participate.
The output preserves deterministic variable ordering based on the order variables first appear across the input datasets.
Required coordinates still trigger ValueError when missing from any dataset involved in the coordinate-aware concat.
acceptance_criteria: When concatenating datasets where one input lacks a data variable present in another, the operation should succeed and the result should include that variable with missing values in the absent positions.
When multiple datasets each omit different data variables, the result should contain the union of those variables and place missing values only in the slices contributed by datasets that lacked them.
When concatenation is performed with a non-default fill_value, missing portions introduced by absent variables should reflect that fill behavior in the observable result.
When a participating coordinate is absent from one or more datasets under coordinate-inclusive concat settings, xarray.concat() should raise ValueError.
When concatenating the same datasets in different orders, the result should preserve a deterministic variable order derived from input appearance rather than failing or producing unstable ordering.
When one or more inputs are empty or contain only a subset of variables, concatenation should still produce a valid dataset consistent with the relaxed data-variable matching rules.

task_1.title: Raise runtime support floor to Python 3.9 and newer dependency minimums
task_1.description: The 2023.2.0 update removes support for Python 3.8 and older dependency combinations, aligning the library with newer minimum versions for core packages such as NumPy, pandas, dask, distributed, h5netcdf, lxml, and numba. As a result, compatibility behavior is standardized around these newer dependency baselines, including backend handling and warning or error behavior that previously depended on legacy versions.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that upgrading to 2023.2.0 is treated as a runtime compatibility update: the library should only be used on Python 3.9+ with the documented minimum dependency versions, and users should observe the standardized behavior associated with those supported versions.

expectation.grounded: xarray 2023.2.0 should require Python 3.9 or newer and minimum versions including numpy 1.21, pandas 1.4, dask 2022.1, distributed 2022.1, h5netcdf 0.13, lxml 4.7, and numba 0.55. On supported versions, dask-backed assignment through xarray should be available for the supported indexer forms without the legacy unsupported-dask TypeError path, H5NetCDFStore should consistently pass decode_vlen_strings to h5netcdf, CFTimeIndex slicing and related pandas interop should follow the newer pandas API surface, and complex-number NetCDF writes through the h5netcdf backend should only round-trip when invalid_netcdf is explicitly enabled.
expectation.conceptual: After upgrading, the package should run only on the newer supported Python and dependency stack. Behavior that previously varied across older dependency versions should become consistent: supported dask installations should allow the documented assignment operations, supported h5netcdf installations should use modern string-decoding behavior, and operations that rely on modern pandas or NumPy behavior should expose the warnings and errors of those supported versions rather than preserving legacy compatibility branches.

constraints.grounded: Do not preserve compatibility promises for Python 3.8 or dependency versions below the new minimums. Keep existing public behavior for supported environments, including the remaining NotImplementedError for dask outer assignment with multiple array indices, the requirement to set invalid_netcdf=True for complex values with the h5netcdf backend, and modern NumPy error behavior when padding integer data with NaN. Changes should describe observable API behavior only and not imply internal migration steps.
constraints.conceptual: The upgrade should narrow the supported environment without changing the intended behavior on the newly supported stack. Unsupported old-version fallbacks should not be treated as regressions, but current users should still see stable, predictable results and clear failure modes for unsupported operations.

behavior: Python 3.8 is no longer a supported runtime; Python 3.9 or newer is required.
Minimum supported versions for key dependencies are raised, including NumPy, pandas, dask, distributed, h5netcdf, lxml, and numba.
Dask-backed xarray objects rely on supported dask item-assignment behavior instead of exposing the previous fallback error for older dask releases.
Assignment into dask-backed data still rejects outer indexing that uses multiple array indices with a NotImplementedError.
Resample operations that use pandas-backed indexes no longer hide pandas deprecation warnings tied to deprecated Grouper parameters such as base or loffset.
h5netcdf-backed opening uses decode_vlen_strings consistently on supported h5netcdf versions.
Writing complex-valued data with the h5netcdf backend only succeeds when invalid_netcdf is explicitly enabled; otherwise it should fail rather than silently round-trip.
Operations that depend on modern NumPy behavior, such as padding integer arrays with NaN constant values, should raise an error instead of producing legacy sentinel-filled output.
acceptance_criteria: When the library is installed on Python 3.8, the upgrade should be considered unsupported rather than expected to work.
When the library is installed on Python 3.9+ with dependency versions at or above the documented minimums, core functionality should run without relying on legacy compatibility branches.
When assigning into a dask-backed xarray object using supported basic, vectorized, or single-array outer indexing, the assignment should succeed on supported dask versions.
When assigning into a dask-backed xarray object using outer indexing with multiple array indices, it should raise NotImplementedError.
When writing complex-valued data through the h5netcdf backend with invalid_netcdf=True, the data should round-trip successfully.
When writing complex-valued data through the h5netcdf backend without enabling invalid_netcdf, the operation should fail.
When resampling on pandas-backed datetime indexes with deprecated grouping parameters, users should be able to observe the underlying pandas warning behavior instead of xarray suppressing it.
When padding an integer-valued array with NaN constant values, the operation should raise a ValueError on the supported NumPy baseline.

task_4.title: Respect keep_attrs in Dataset binary operations
task_4.description: Upgrading to 2023.2.0 fixes a behavioral inconsistency in xarray so Dataset binary operations now honor the global keep_attrs option. When attribute preservation is enabled, the resulting Dataset keeps the left-hand Dataset attributes instead of dropping them.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that Dataset binary operations preserve dataset-level attributes when attribute retention is enabled, so Dataset behavior matches user expectations and remains consistent with other xarray container types.

expectation.grounded: In xarray 2023.2.0, Dataset binary operators must consult the global keep_attrs option set via xr.set_options(keep_attrs=...). When keep_attrs is True, a binary operation such as Dataset + Dataset returns a Dataset whose attrs equal the left-hand Dataset attrs. When keep_attrs is False, the result attrs remain empty rather than merging attrs from both operands.
expectation.conceptual: Binary arithmetic on Dataset objects should respect the library's attribute-preservation setting. If attribute retention is enabled, the result should keep the original dataset metadata from the primary input; if it is disabled, the operation should continue to produce a result without preserved metadata.

constraints.grounded: The change is limited to Dataset binary operation attribute handling and must not alter the computed data variables, alignment behavior, or the existing keep_attrs=False outcome. Result attrs must not be combined from both operands; the preserved attrs come from the left-hand Dataset when retention is enabled.
constraints.conceptual: The fix should only affect whether metadata is retained during Dataset-to-Dataset arithmetic. It must not change numerical results or introduce new metadata-combination behavior beyond preserving the source dataset metadata when requested.

behavior: Dataset binary operations now honor the global keep_attrs setting.
With keep_attrs enabled, the resulting Dataset preserves dataset-level attrs from the left-hand operand.
With keep_attrs disabled, Dataset binary operations continue to return results without preserved attrs.
The update resolves a prior inconsistency where Dataset arithmetic ignored keep_attrs even though related xarray object types respected it.
acceptance_criteria: When two Dataset objects with attrs are combined under xr.set_options(keep_attrs=True), the resulting Dataset should retain the attrs of the left-hand Dataset.
When the same binary operation is performed under xr.set_options(keep_attrs=False), the resulting Dataset should have no preserved attrs.
When Dataset binary operations are executed, the data values and variable structure should remain unchanged apart from the documented attribute-retention behavior.
When users rely on keep_attrs for xarray objects, Dataset binary arithmetic should behave consistently with that option instead of ignoring it.

task_5.title: Validate missing output_sizes in dask apply_ufunc
task_5.description: The update tightens and clarifies validation for xarray.apply_ufunc() when used with dask='parallelized'. If an output core dimension is new to the outputs or is excluded from alignment and therefore requires an explicit size, the call should fail with a clear output_sizes-related ValueError instead of allowing the invalid configuration to proceed with a poor or misleading error.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that using xarray.apply_ufunc() with Dask parallelization reports a clear validation error whenever output core dimensions require explicit sizes but output_sizes is not provided.

expectation.grounded: When xarray.apply_ufunc() is called with dask='parallelized', every output core dimension that is not inherited from the effective input dimensions, including dimensions listed in exclude_dims, must have a corresponding entry in output_sizes. If such a size is missing, the call should raise ValueError and clearly indicate that output_sizes is required for that dimension.
expectation.conceptual: Parallelized ufunc execution should consistently reject underspecified output shapes. If the library cannot infer the size of an output dimension from the usable inputs, the user should get an immediate, explicit error telling them to supply output_sizes.

constraints.grounded: Dimensions that are validly inferred from input core dimensions should continue to work without output_sizes. The validation should apply specifically to Dask-parallelized apply_ufunc() calls and should cover cases where output and input reuse the same dimension names but those dimensions are excluded from alignment or inference.
constraints.conceptual: The fix must improve error reporting without breaking calls whose output shapes are already well-defined. It should close gaps where shape validation was skipped because dimension names happened to match, even though the sizes were not actually inferable.

behavior: apply_ufunc() with dask='parallelized' now treats excluded output core dimensions as requiring explicit output_sizes when their sizes cannot be inferred.
Reusing the same dimension names between input_core_dims and output_core_dims no longer bypasses missing output_sizes validation if those dimensions are excluded.
Invalid shape specifications fail early with ValueError rather than proceeding to a less informative downstream failure mode.
The error signal is specifically tied to the absence of output_sizes for the affected output dimension.
acceptance_criteria: When a Dask-parallelized apply_ufunc() call produces an output core dimension that is not inferable from input dimensions, it should raise ValueError unless output_sizes provides that dimension's size.
When output_core_dims reuse names from input_core_dims but those dimensions are included in exclude_dims, omitting output_sizes should still raise ValueError.
When all required output dimensions are either inferable from inputs or explicitly declared in output_sizes, the apply_ufunc() call should continue to run successfully.
When the validation fails, the reported error should make it clear that output_sizes is the missing requirement.

task_6.title: Handle xarray-added encodings in Dataset.to_zarr
task_6.description: The xarray 2023.2.0 upgrade fixes a zarr export failure in xarray.Dataset.to_zarr() by ignoring internal encoding metadata that xarray adds when datasets are read. This allows datasets opened from existing sources to be written to zarr using copied variable encodings without failing on unsupported encoding keys.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that datasets opened in xarray can be written with Dataset.to_zarr() even when variable encodings copied from the loaded dataset include xarray-added metadata that is not part of the zarr encoding API.

expectation.grounded: When xarray.Dataset.to_zarr() receives per-variable encoding dictionaries derived from Variable.encoding or DataArray.encoding on a dataset that was previously read by xarray, the zarr backend should ignore the xarray-added encoding keys source and original_shape before validating zarr encoding options. The write should proceed normally instead of raising ValueError for those keys.
expectation.conceptual: Writing an already-opened dataset to zarr should work when callers reuse the dataset's existing variable encodings. Internal metadata added during reading should not be treated as an invalid user encoding option or block the export.

constraints.grounded: Only the known xarray-generated encoding keys source and original_shape are treated as safe to ignore for zarr export. Existing validation of unsupported zarr encoding parameters must remain in effect for other invalid keys, and valid zarr encoding options must continue to be honored.
constraints.conceptual: The fix should be narrowly scoped to internal read-time metadata and must not weaken normal validation of genuinely unsupported zarr encoding settings.

behavior: xarray.Dataset.to_zarr() no longer fails solely because copied variable encodings contain source.
xarray.Dataset.to_zarr() no longer fails solely because copied variable encodings contain original_shape.
The zarr backend continues validating encoding entries and may still raise ValueError for unsupported keys other than the known internal metadata fields.
Datasets loaded from existing files can be round-tripped to zarr using reused variable encodings for data variables.
acceptance_criteria: When a dataset is opened with xarray and each data variable's existing encoding is copied into the encoding argument of Dataset.to_zarr(), the write should complete successfully if the only non-zarr keys are source and original_shape.

When copied encodings include valid zarr options together with source and original_shape, the valid zarr options should still be applied and the write should not fail because of those internal metadata keys.
When an encoding dictionary passed to Dataset.to_zarr() contains another unsupported key that is not part of the allowed zarr encoding API, the operation should still fail with a validation error.
Round-tripping a representative dataset from an existing on-disk source to zarr using reused per-variable encodings should succeed without requiring callers to manually strip xarray-added metadata.

task_7.title: Document flox support for groupby and resample aggregations
task_7.description: The update expands user-facing documentation for xarray groupby and resample aggregation methods to explain that the optional flox package can accelerate these operations, especially for dask-backed data, that xarray will use flox automatically when it is installed, and that flox-specific keyword arguments can be passed through supported aggregation APIs.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that users upgrading can discover that groupby and resample aggregations support optional flox acceleration, understand that it is used automatically when available, and know how flox-specific options affect observable aggregation behavior.

expectation.grounded: Public xarray aggregation APIs exposed on DataArrayGroupBy, DatasetGroupBy, DataArrayResample, and DatasetResample should document that installing flox can significantly speed up groupby and resampling reductions, especially for dask-backed arrays. The documented contract should state that xarray uses flox by default when it is installed, that flox-specific keyword arguments may be passed through `**kwargs`, and that `method="cohorts"` is the default documented method choice, with other methods potentially preferable for groupby and `method="blockwise"` specifically called out as an alternative for resampling.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be told, in the main aggregation method documentation, that an optional acceleration backend is available for grouped and resampled reductions, that it is picked up automatically when present, and that callers can tune its behavior through supported keyword arguments. The guidance should also explain the default recommended method and note when an alternative method may perform better.

constraints.grounded: This upgrade should not alter the existing callable surface or reduction semantics of groupby or resample methods. Numeric-only reductions must continue to document their existing non-numeric-variable behavior alongside the new flox guidance, and the flox notes must remain consistent across generated aggregation docstrings for both DataArray and Dataset variants.
constraints.conceptual: The change is informational and must not break existing grouped or resampled workflows. Existing behavior descriptions should remain intact, and the new guidance should appear consistently anywhere users would reasonably look for aggregation method documentation.

behavior: GroupBy aggregation documentation now explicitly states that flox can significantly speed up grouped reductions, especially with dask-backed data.
Resample aggregation documentation now explicitly states that flox can significantly speed up resampling reductions, especially with dask-backed data.
Supported aggregation docstrings now state that xarray uses flox automatically when flox is installed.
Supported aggregation docstrings now state that flox-specific options may be passed via `**kwargs`.
GroupBy aggregation guidance now documents `method="cohorts"` as the default method choice and notes that other methods may be better in some cases.
Resample aggregation guidance now documents `method="cohorts"` as the default method choice and highlights `method="blockwise"` as a possible better alternative for some workloads.
Methods that already document removal of non-numeric variables for numeric-only reductions continue to surface that behavior together with the new flox notes.
acceptance_criteria: When a user reads any documented DataArray or Dataset groupby aggregation method, it should state that flox can accelerate the operation and is used automatically if installed.
When a user reads any documented DataArray or Dataset resample aggregation method, it should state that flox can accelerate the operation and is used automatically if installed.
When a user checks the documented parameters for supported grouped or resampled reductions, it should be clear that flox-specific keyword arguments may be passed through `**kwargs`.

When a user looks for method-selection guidance in groupby aggregation docs, it should identify `method="cohorts"` as the default documented choice and note that alternatives may be preferable in some cases.

When a user looks for method-selection guidance in resample aggregation docs, it should identify `method="cohorts"` as the default documented choice and mention `method="blockwise"` as a possible better alternative.
When a user reads a numeric-only groupby or resample reduction docstring, it should still retain the existing note that non-numeric variables are removed before reduction.
